title: Punctual purity for regular log-smooth schemes over a trait
statement:
For a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. If $W$ is a regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], say that $W$ is punctually pure at $w\in W$ when, for $W_w=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $d_w=\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and its closed-point inclusion $j_w:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\hookrightarrow W_w$, the Kummer fundamental-class map
$$A_{\kappa(w)}\longrightarrow j_w^!A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$$
of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Say that $W$ is punctually pure when this holds at every point. Local rings and residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field], affine spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

A trait here is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ for a discrete valuation ring: a Noetherian local domain of dimension one whose maximal ideal is principal. A complete strictly henselian trait has $R$ complete for its maximal-ideal topology and henselian with separably closed residue field (henselian means that every simple root over the residue field of a monic polynomial over $R$ lifts to a root over $R$). Mixed characteristic means that $\operatorname{Frac}R$ has characteristic zero and the residue field has positive characteristic.

Use fs log structures, charts and log morphisms as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. The canonical log structure on a trait is the subsheaf of $\mathcal O_S$ of sections invertible on its generic point; a uniformizer gives its chart $\mathbf N\to R$. In this statement, log smooth over that trait has its fs chart meaning: etale locally on source and target there are compatible charts $\mathbf N\to P$ with $P$ fine saturated, the group map injective with torsion in its cokernel of finite order invertible on the source, such that the induced scheme map to $S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[\mathbf N]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$ is smooth. Here $\mathbf Z[P]$ is the free abelian group on $P$ with multiplication induced by the monoid law.

Let $S$ be a trait on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let $(V,M)\to S$ be an fs log-smooth morphism with $V$ regular Noetherian. Then $V$ is punctually pure.

source.place: Expose XVI, Theorem 3.6.2 and chart Proposition 3.6.3, printed p.252; reduction by Proposition 3.6.5 to the monomial schemes of Proposition 3.5.12, printed pp.250--253. The canonical log structure is Definition 3.6.1.

proof.text: Fix $v\in V$ and a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$. Apply [lem-per-regular-log-smooth-monomial-chart] with $X=V$ and the given fs log-smooth morphism to the canonically logged trait. It gives a regular affine Noetherian $U$, an etale $a:U\to V$, a point $u$ with $a(u)=v$, and an etale $S$-morphism $b:U\to T$, where $T=\operatorname{Spec}(R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(\prod_i T_i^{e_i}-\pi))$, $n\geq1$ and the nonnegative $e_i$ are not all zero.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.6.5, printed p.253, using Proposition 3.6.3, p.252.

proof.text: The same $R,\pi,n$ and tuple $(e_i)$ satisfy [lem-per-monomial-trait-punctual-purity]: $R$ is a discrete valuation ring, $\ell$ is invertible in it, and the exponents are nonnegative and not all zero. Thus this very $T$ is regular Noetherian and punctually pure. In particular it is punctually pure at $t=b(u)$.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definition 3.5.11 and Proposition 3.5.12, printed p.250; concluding reduction on p.253.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-punctual-purity-etale-locality] to $b:U\to T$ at $u$: its pointwise equivalence gives purity of $U$ at $u$ from purity of $T$ at $t$. Apply the same equivalence to $a:U\to V$ at $u$: purity of $U$ at $u$ gives purity of $V$ at $v=a(u)$. Both applications are between regular Noetherian schemes: $U$ comes from step 1, $T$ from step 2, and $V$ from the hypothesis. The image of the unit $\ell\in R$ is a unit on each $S$-scheme, so the coefficient hypothesis holds throughout. Since $v$ was arbitrary, $V$ is punctually pure, including vacuously when $V$ is empty.

Source checked: ILO XVI p.244 (Def 3.2.1-3.2.2), pp.250-251 (Def 3.5.11, Prop 3.5.12), p.252 (Def 3.6.1, Thm 3.6.2, Prop 3.6.3) and p.253 (Prop 3.6.5, whose last sentence derives Thm 3.6.2 from 3.6.5 and 3.5.12). The item's punctual-purity paragraph is word for word the first paragraph of the monomial and locality nodes, and its log-smooth paragraph is word for word the chart node's, so the coefficient category, Kummer map and dimension normalization are literally shared. Step 1: the chart node's hypotheses (fs log-smooth over the canonically logged trait, X regular Noetherian, a point and a uniformizer) all hold, and it gives U, an etale a, a point u, and an etale S-map b to T with n>=1 and exponents not all zero. Step 2: the monomial node's hypotheses (same R, pi and tuple, ell invertible in R, arbitrary trait) hold, and it gives T regular and pure at b(u). Step 3: the locality iff is applied backwards along b (U and T regular) and forwards along a (V regular); ell is a unit on every S-scheme. Edge cases checked: V empty, generic-fibre points, n=1 with e=(1) giving T=S, zero exponents and exponents divisible by ell or p. All inputs are in the same unit, so there are no tool_uses; there are no new nodes, no cycle, no SGA, and no duplicate of Thm 3.6.2 in the DAG.
